paragraph_content.content: Stabilizing industry TAM driven by rising renovation demand offsetting new builds contraction

Following a 20% contraction in industry TAM (vs. 70% erosion in market cap for our 4 covered BM companies, Yuhong, Skshu, Vasen and BNBM) between 2021-25, our analysis now suggests a N-T pivot with record pent-up demand and increasing secondary sales to support a stabilizing TAM outlook. In the long run, we anticipate a return to peak TAM levels, to provide tailwind for both earnings growth and multiple expansion.
Summary of TAM by four building material sectors
Aggressive 2C retail expansion, deepened lower-tier/rural penetration, and overseas exploration

The four BM companies are adopting three primary strategies: 1) aggressive 2C retail expansion; 2) deepening penetration into lower-tier and rural markets; and 3) broadening product portfolios. We estimate these initiatives will drive almost the entire topline growth through 2025-28E, with the greatest impact projected for Skshu. In addition, Yuhong has demonstrated solid execution in international markets.

paragraph_content.content: Improving as one of the benefits from shifting channel to retail business

Building materials prices (especially waterproofing and paint) have already started to increase on recent cost inflation but raw materials are starting to rollover turning that price into margin. We expect GPM for the four BM companies to remain stable or expand through 2027E, driven by favorable mix shift toward the 2C segment, and we forecast a coverage-wide GPM improvement of 1~3pp from 2025 to end-28E.

paragraph_content.content: Bottoming out driven by channel shift and SG&A optimization

As the strategic pivots gain traction, we expect profitability and CROCI for the sector to bottom out with average 4pp NM and 3pp CROCI expansion for 25A to 28E for the four companies with Skshu positioned for the strongest recovery and Vasen the most modest. Overall, we expect 9-29% EPS CAGRs for the four names over 2026E-2028E vs. on median -8% in 2025.

paragraph_content.content: Our 12-m TPs imply 13%-53% upside for the sector; Buy Yuhong and Skshu

Looking ahead, we project a 12-m forward EV/GCI multiple expansion of 0.1x, supported by a 1pp improvement in CROCI relative to 2026E levels, and implying 13%-53% upside for the sector. For our Buy-rated names (Yuhong and Skshu), we anticipate more pronounced expansion of +0.3x, driven by stronger CROCI gains, and implying 47%/53% upside respectively.

Skshu603737.SSBuyOur 12-m EV/GCI vs. CROCI-based target price is Rmb35.90Downside risks:1) Weaker-than-expected execution in new retail businesses development, especially in Mashangzhu store count expansion and deepening Beautiful rural penetration, resulting in retail-channel topline miss; 2) weaker-than-expected product ASP and margins due to intensified competition among large peers and sluggish consumer confidence; 3) slower-than-expected SG&A expense optimization progress due to missteps in redundant salesperson headcount reduction and heavier-than-expected expenditure in promoting fast-growing retail segments; 4) an unexpected surge in raw material (over 80% of Skshu's COGS) prices driven by upstream oil price increase, leading to margin squeeze. Despite years of efforts to improve procurement and inventory management systems, Skshu still has limited bargaining power against suppliers.
Vasen002372.SZNeutralOur 12-m EV/GCI vs. CROCI-based target price is Rmb9.3Up/downside risks:1) Faster-than-expected cross-selling of waterproof coating and other new products, or slower-than-expected "concentric circles" businesses growth; 2) consumer confidence recovery which accelerates home renovation/unleash the pent-up demand for pipe replacement, or more-prolonged-than-expected consumer sentiment weakness resulting in further postponement of household pipe replacement. 3) stronger/weaker-than-expected share expansion in China's plastic pipe market especially in areas outside and lower-tier markets surrounding Vasen's traditionally strong YRD regions; 4) faster/slower-than-expected overseas business expansion, especially in South East Asia; 5) an unexpected drop/surge in raw material prices driven by upstream oil and coal prices decreases/increases; 6) faster-than-expected implementation of urban renewal, especially underground pipeline renovation on the back of intensified central government financial support, resulting in upbeat project-channel order recovery.
BNBM000786.SZNeutralOur 12-m EV/GCI vs. CROCI-based target price is Rmb22.4Up/downside risks:1) higher/lower-than-expected domestic property completions; 2) stronger/weaker-than-expected regional penetration or nationwide capacity expansion by new entrants, leading to more/less fierce price and volume competition; 3) better/worse-than-expected execution of internal realignments of gypsum board brands, in terms of coordinated price hikes and cost efficiency improvements; 4) higher/lower-than-expected revenue growth and margins delivered by new business verticals (waterproofing, coatings, metal framing), subject to stronger/weaker-than-expected cross-selling opportunity capture; 5) higher/lower-than-expected raw material and energy costs, especially in terms of paper which accounts for ~35%-40% of BNBM's gypsum board COGS, and coal and power which together make up ~15%-20% of segment COGS; 6) better/worse-than-expected operational synergies yielded by M&A integrations (especially for the Carpoly brand).

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
